# RoboARC

> RoboARC is a benchmark of 90 physical puzzles for robotic manipulation under spatial constraints: six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo, each task in a Privileged and a Standard regime. Paper: "RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints" (2026; arXiv version coming soon), from Northwestern University, Microsoft, UC Berkeley and Carnegie Mellon University. Project page: https://roboarc.embodied-first-exam.ai/

The question RoboARC asks: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? Each task is a physical puzzle. In one, two claws are hooked through each other: pulling only jams them, and they come apart only when turned in the right order. Others ask a robot to bring a spiky ball out of a cage, untie a knot, thread a rope through rings in order, assemble IKEA furniture or fold a blanket.

## Key facts

- RoboARC is one of the nine new suites of the Embodied First Exam (https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/, arXiv 2611.12177), an agentic robotics benchmark in which coding agents control robots; RoboARC is its spatial-constraint puzzle suite (https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/roboarc/).
- Scale: 90 tasks: 78 puzzles in 19 families, and 12 IKEA furniture scenes.
- Six constraint types. Rigid materials: Interlocking (23 tasks), Narrow passage (13), Assembly (20, including the 12 IKEA scenes). Soft materials: Untangling (13), Threading (11), Shape control (10).
- Three robots, simulated in MuJoCo: ALOHA 2 (two arms), a Franka arm with a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, and two Franka Pandas.
- Two regimes for coding agents. Standard: the agent sends action chunks and receives RGB-D images, joint readings and the instruction, without resets. Privileged: it sends actions, may reset, and receives the full simulator state. One grader replays the physics of every run.
- Results on all 90 tasks (the paper's main table; mean of 3 runs ± standard deviation, 270 trials per agent and regime): the seven coding agents solve between 4.1% and 42.6% of the tasks in the Standard regime, and between 4.4% and 85.6% in the Privileged regime.
- VLA policies, as a reference: π0.5, MolmoAct2, GR00T N1.7 and Cosmos3-Nano-Policy, zero-shot in the Standard regime on 18 puzzles (13 narrow passage, 5 threading), 3 runs per puzzle, solve none of them. The gripper touched the task object in 31.5% to 61.1% of their episodes.
- Every coding-agent run is published: 3,780 runs (7 agents on the 90 tasks, both regimes, 3 runs each), step by step: what the agent wrote, ran and saw, and what the verifier decided.

## Leaderboard: Standard regime (success rate on all 90 tasks, mean of 3 runs ± s.d.)

- GPT-6 Astra (Codex, xhigh): 42.6% ± 5.1
- GPT-6.1 Sol (Codex, xhigh): 34.8% ± 5.0
- Gemini 4 Argon (Antigravity, high): 30.7% ± 4.6
- Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, xhigh): 29.3% ± 1.7
- Kimi 3.1 Pro (Kimi Code, max): 7.0% ± 1.7
- DeepSeek v4.1 Flash (DeepSeek Harness, high): 5.6% ± 1.9
- GLM 5.3 Flash (Claude Code, high): 4.1% ± 2.8

## Leaderboard: Privileged regime (success rate on all 90 tasks, mean of 3 runs ± s.d.)

- GPT-6 Astra (Codex, xhigh): 85.6% ± 4.4
- GPT-6.1 Sol (Codex, xhigh): 81.1% ± 1.1
- Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, xhigh): 80.7% ± 0.6
- Gemini 4 Argon (Antigravity, high): 73.3% ± 4.0
- Kimi 3.1 Pro (Kimi Code, max): 31.5% ± 3.6
- DeepSeek v4.1 Flash (DeepSeek Harness, high): 10.7% ± 1.3
- GLM 5.3 Flash (Claude Code, high): 4.4% ± 2.2
